newsitem.title: USA: US Justice sues Rochester Gas over university pact.
newsitem.headline: US Justice sues Rochester Gas over university pact.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday it sued Rochester Gas and Electric over an "anti-competitive" agreement the utility reached with the University of Rochester.
The department charged that the pact prevents RG&E customers from receiving low-cost electricity.
The department's antitrust division said the agreement deprives some RB&E customers of alternative low-cost electricity, forcing them to pay more for their electricity.

"As the electric industry becomes increasingly deregulated, vigorous antitrust enforcement is absolutely essential to ensure that consumers benefit from competition," said Joel Klein, acting assistant attorney general.
"This case should be a wake-up call to electric utilities. We will not tolerate private arrangements designed to thwart the introduction of competition into this important industry."
The department charged that RG&E made threats and offered financial rewards to induce the university to abandon its plan to build a new, efficient power plant in the Rochester area.
The agreement also prevented the university from participating in any projects that would provide other current RG&E custoemrs with energy from any other utility, according to the department.

The department's complaint was filed in U.S. District Court for the Western District of New York. It charged that RG&E threatened to cut off certain research grants to the university if the plant were built.

The department asked the court to bar RG&E from enforcing the existing agreement or offering anything of value to induce a competitor not to compete with RG&E in the sale of electricity or the generation of electricity for that purpose.
